Treatment summary
Patient presented following a sideswipe collision that occurred while the other vehicle was changing lanes.
Examination revealed localized tenderness and swelling over the distal radius of the affected wrist, with reduced grip
strength on the injured side. Imaging was consistent with a wrist fracture. Neurovascular status of the hand was
intact, and the remaining orthopedic and neurological tests were within normal limits. The patient has no known prior
injury to this wrist or the surrounding area. Over three visits, the patient was treated with immobilization, pain
management, and a graduated home exercise program. Treatment followed a typical course, and symptoms steadily
improved, so care was tapered off at the final visit. At this time, it remains unclear whether the fracture is entirely
attributable to this incident, and the billing records for two similar charges on the same date of service are under
review.

Rate each feature below that THIS page gives evidence about. Leave out a feature the page
says nothing about. The ratings are listed from least to most suspicious.
- injury_crash_fit: Does the claimed injury fit the type and force of the crash? Allowed: Strong, Reasonable, Unclear, Inconsistent.
- treatment_growth: Did the treatment grow beyond what this injury needs? Allowed: Normal, Elevated, Disproportionate, Extreme.
- objective_support: Do objective tests (imaging, exam findings) support the complaints? Allowed: Strong, Partial, Predominantly subjective, Contradicted.
- pre_existing_condition: Did an earlier condition of the same body area add to the complaints? Allowed: None, Minor, Material, Predominant.
- duplicate_billing: Was the same service, visit or part billed twice? Allowed: None, Possible, Confirmed.

- "confidence": "High", "Medium" or "Low" (how clearly the page shows it),
